intent: A capital you climb to: three city silhouettes to scale, a real photograph of the city rising out of the map, a pin on the seat of government with the two-capitals twist, and the thin-air close on the football pitch.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country has the HIGHEST capital city?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country has the highest capital city?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Bolivia. La Paz, its seat of government, sits 3,640 metres up, higher than any other capital.

lines.direction: ease back over the Altiplano; three skyline silhouettes rise on 'Ecuador' — Kathmandu a stub, Quito a step, La Paz a tower; the Ecuadorian flag-ball thinks on 'Nepal'; a mountain sticker on 'only' as Bolivia pulses
lines.text: Ecuador's capital is about 2,850 metres. Nepal's, under the Himalaya, only 1,400.

lines.direction: drift south-east; a twist sticker on 'twist' as the La Paz photograph rises out of Bolivia; the Sucre pin and tag on 'Sucre'; a plane sticker and the El Alto tag on 'airport' as Bolivia pulses
lines.text: A twist: the constitutional capital is Sucre, far lower down. And the airport sits even higher, above the city.

lines.direction: tighten on La Paz; the THIN AIR card on 'air'; a lungs sticker on 'oxygen'; a football sticker on 'gasp'; the Bolivian flag-ball grins on 'loses' as Bolivia pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: Up here the air holds a third less oxygen. Visiting football teams gasp; the home side rarely loses.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A capital above the clouds. Follow us.
